verdict: PASS on the MECHANISM - but the focused court's proof of this property is SELF-REFERENTIAL (see 08_COURT_COVERAGE_GAPS_ADDENDUM.json GAP-3)
method: called assert_receipt_does_not_authorize(receipt, purpose) for EVERY purpose in FORBIDDEN_AUTHORIZED_PURPOSES against a real receipt containing an ADMITTED source, then inspected the per-decision power flags

E1_all_fourteen_purposes_refused.note: this matches the commission's eleven named powers plus three additional prohibited surfaces the module enumerates

court_self_reference_caveat.finding: the court parametrises over list(M.FORBIDDEN_AUTHORIZED_PURPOSES) - the same tuple the function checks - so a truncated production tuple would collect fewer cases and still pass
court_self_reference_caveat.deeper_finding: assert_receipt_does_not_authorize NEVER READS ITS `receipt` ARGUMENT (verified: the body validates `purpose`, then raises on membership in the forbidden tuple). The court therefore proves the FUNCTION refuses its own list, not that the RECEIPT carries no authority.
court_self_reference_caveat.what_actually_carries_the_property: DECISION_MATRIX, whose may_* flags are False for every decision - which I verified by value inspection, independently of the court
court_self_reference_caveat.my_evidence_still_holds: I called the function for all 14 purposes on a real receipt and got 14/14 refusals; the mechanism is confirmed. The caveat is about what the COURT proves, not about whether the property holds.

E2_decision_matrix_power_flags.finding: every may_* flag is False for every non-ADMITTED decision; on ADMITTED only the three admission-scoped flags are True (positive_admission, may_enter_source_set, may_constrain_downstream_query_scope)
E2_decision_matrix_power_flags.significance: even the strongest positive outcome cannot serve as conditioning, geometry transformation or individual inference. This is the 'eligibility is not conditioning' boundary holding at the data-structure level.

E3_target_use_permission_cannot_become_a.evidence: may_grant_target_use_permission is False on all ten decision rows; the request declares target_use_permission_refs_are_bound_input_not_a_grant = True; TARGET_USE_PERMISSION_GRANT is in FORBIDDEN_AUTHORIZED_PURPOSES and was refused

E4_currentness_and_F8.evidence: CURRENTNESS_AUTHORITY and F8_GEOMETRY_OR_DISTRIBUTION_TRANSFORM both refused; may_condition_F8 False; the module forecloses the specific HQ203/H-D frontier question by refusing to be conditioning authority at all

structural_vs_declarative.finding: the refusal is STRUCTURAL, not merely declarative: assert_receipt_does_not_authorize is a function that raises, and the power flags are a closed matrix keyed by decision. A caller cannot obtain authorisation by asserting it; the API has no grant path.
structural_vs_declarative.residual: the receipt is a plain immutable dataclass, so a caller could in principle ignore the assert helper and read .as_dict() themselves. That is a caller-misconduct boundary, not an authority overreach: the module never ISSUES the power, and every machine-readable declaration on the receipt states it does not.
